sanskrit: tato bherīś ca śaṅkhāṃś ca śataśaś caiva puṣkarān vādayām āsur avyagrāḥ puruṣā rājaśāsanāt
english: Then, by royal command, men without distraction beat kettledrums and conch-shells and kettle-drums by the hundreds.

sanskrit: siṃhanādāś ca vividhā vāhanānāṃ ca nisvanāḥ prādurāsann anabhre ca varṣaṃ rudhirakardamam
english: Diverse lion-roars arose and the cries of beasts of burden, and from a cloudless sky there fell a rain of blood and mud.

sanskrit: nirghātāḥ pṛthivīkampā gajabṛṃhitanisvanāḥ āsaṃś ca sarvayodhānāṃ pātayanto manāṃsy uta
english: Thunderbolts, earthquakes, and the screaming of elephants arose and struck terror into the hearts of all warriors.

sanskrit: vācaś cāpy aśarīriṇyo divaś colkāḥ prapedire śivāś ca bhayavedinyo nedur dīptasvarā bhṛśam
english: Bodiless voices were heard, and meteors fell from the sky; jackals that foretell evil cried out loudly with blazing voices again and again.

sanskrit: senāpatye yadā rājā gāṅgeyam abhiṣiktavān tadaitāny ugrarūpāṇi abhavañ śataśo nṛpa
english: When the king consecrated Bhishma, son of the Ganges, as commander of the army, O king, these terrible omens manifested by the hundreds.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā bhīṣmaṃ parabalārdanam vācayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhān niṣkair gobhiś ca bhūriśaḥ
english: Then, having made Bhishma, the crusher of enemy forces, commander, and having caused the foremost brahmins to recite blessings and having given them golden coins and cattle in abundance,

sanskrit: vardhamāno jayāśīrbhir niryayau sainikair vṛtaḥ āpageyaṃ puraskṛtya bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitas tadā skandhāvāreṇa mahatā kurukṣetraṃ jagāma ha
english: swelling with benedictions of victory, Duryodhana marched out surrounded by soldiers, with his brothers and with Bhishma at the fore, and went with a great army to Kurukshetra.

sanskrit: parikramya kurukṣetraṃ karṇena saha kauravaḥ śibiraṃ māpayām āsa same deśe narādhipaḥ
english: Having circumambulated Kurukshetra together with Karna, the Kaurava king had his camp measured out on level ground.

sanskrit: madhurānūṣare deśe prabhūtayavasendhane yathaiva hāstinapuraṃ tadvac chibiram ābabhau
english: In a region pleasant and not too saline, rich in barley and fodder, the camp shone just like Hastinapura itself.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca āpageyaṃ mahātmānaṃ bhīṣmaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam pitāmahaṃ bhāratānāṃ dhvajaṃ sarvamahīkṣitām
english: Janamejaya said: When the great-souled Bhishma, son of the river, foremost among weapon-bearers, grandfather of the Bharatas and banner of all kings of the earth,

sanskrit: bṛhaspatisamaṃ buddhyā kṣamayā pṛthivīsamam samudram iva gāmbhīrye himavantam iva sthiram
english: equal to Brihaspati in wisdom, equal to the earth in forbearance, like the ocean in depth, and firm as the Himalayas,

sanskrit: prajāpatim ivaudārye tejasā bhāskaropamam mahendram iva śatrūṇāṃ dhvaṃsanaṃ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: like Prajapati in generosity, like the sun in splendor, and like great Indra in destroying enemies with showers of arrows—

sanskrit: raṇayajñe pratibhaye svābhīle lomaharṣaṇe dīkṣitaṃ cirarātrāya śrutvā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: when king Yudhishthira heard that he had been consecrated for a long time to the sacrifice of battle, dreadful and hair-raising—

sanskrit: kim abravīn mahābāhuḥ sarvadharmaviśāradaḥ bhīmasenārjunau vāpi kṛṣṇo vā pratyapadyata
english: what did the mighty-armed one, skilled in all dharma, say? And what did Bhimasena, Arjuna, or Krishna do in response?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca āpaddharmārthakuśalo mahābuddhir yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sarvān bhrātṝn samānīya vāsudevaṃ ca sātvatam uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Yudhishthira, the great-minded one skilled in the duties of adversity and polity, gathered all his brothers and Vasudeva of the Satvata clan, and, foremost among speakers, said these words with gentle reassurance:

sanskrit: paryākrāmata sainyāni yattās tiṣṭhata daṃśitāḥ pitāmahena vo yuddhaṃ pūrvam eva bhaviṣyati tasmāt saptasu senāsu praṇetṝn mama paśyata
english: "Patrol the armies, stand ready, clad in armor. The battle with your grandfather will come first. Therefore look upon the seven leaders of my forces."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca yathārhati bhavān vaktum asmin kāla upasthite tathedam arthavad vākyam uktaṃ te bharatarṣabha
english: Vasudeva said: "As befits you to speak at this time that has arrived, so too this meaningful speech has been uttered by you, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: rocate me mahābāho kriyatāṃ yad anantaram nāyakās tava senāyām abhiṣicyantu sapta vai
english: "It pleases me, O mighty-armed one. Let what follows be done: let seven commanders be consecrated for your army."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato drupadam ānāyya virāṭaṃ śinipuṃgavam dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pāñcālyaṃ dhṛṣṭaketuṃ ca pārthivam śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca pāñcālyaṃ sahadevaṃ ca māgadham
english: Vaishampayana said: Then, summoning Drupada and Virata and the bull of the Shinis, and Dhrishtadyumna the Panchala prince, and the king Dhrishtaketu, and Shikhandi the Panchala, and Sahadeva the Magadha king,

sanskrit: etān sapta maheṣvāsān vīrān yuddhābhinandinaḥ senāpraṇetṝn vidhivad abhyaṣiñcad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: these seven great archers, heroes who delighted in battle—Yudhishthira consecrated them as army commanders according to rite.

sanskrit: sarvasenāpatiṃ cātra dhṛṣṭadyumnam upādiśat droṇāntahetor utpanno ya iddhāñ jātavedasaḥ
english: And as commander-in-chief over all he appointed Dhrishtadyumna—he who was born from the blazing fire for the very purpose of slaying Drona.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva teṣāṃ tu samastānāṃ mahātmanām senāpatipatiṃ cakre guḍākeśaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: But over all of them assembled, those great-souled ones, he made Gudakesha Dhananjaya the lord of commanders.

sanskrit: arjunasyāpi netā ca saṃyantā caiva vājinām saṃkarṣaṇānujaḥ śrīmān mahābuddhir janārdanaḥ
english: And as guide and charioteer of Arjuna's horses stood the glorious and greatly wise Janardana, younger brother of Sankarshana.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā upasthitaṃ yuddhaṃ samāsannaṃ mahātyayam prāviśad bhavanaṃ rājñaḥ pāṇḍavasya halāyudhaḥ
english: Seeing the battle imminent, the great calamity close at hand, Halayudha entered the dwelling of the Pandava king.

sanskrit: sahākrūraprabhṛtibhir gadasāmbolmukādibhiḥ raukmiṇeyāhukasutaiś cārudeṣṇapurogamaiḥ
english: He came accompanied by Akrura and others, by Gada, Samba, Ulmuka and the rest, by the sons of Rukmini and Ahuka, and with Carudeshna at the fore.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇimukhyair abhigatair vyāghrair iva balotkaṭaiḥ abhigupto mahābāhur marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ
english: Escorted by the chief Vrishnis who came like mighty tigers, the great-armed one was protected as Vasava is by the Maruts.

sanskrit: nīlakauśeyavasanaḥ kailāsaśikharopamaḥ siṃhakhelagatiḥ śrīmān madaraktāntalocanaḥ
english: Clad in dark silk garments, resembling a peak of mount Kailasa, moving with the leisurely gait of a lion, glorious, with eyes reddened at the corners by wine—

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmarājaś ca keśavaś ca mahādyutiḥ udatiṣṭhat tadā pārtho bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
english: seeing him, the king of dharma and the greatly radiant Keshava rose, and so did the son of Pritha the terrible-actioned Vrikodara.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvadhanvā ye cānye rājānas tatra ke cana pūjayāṃ cakrur abhyetya te sma sarve halāyudham
english: The Gandiva-bowman and whatever other kings were there—all of them approached and honored Halayudha.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ pāṇḍavo rājā kare pasparśa pāṇinā vāsudevapurogās tu sarva evābhyavādayan
english: Then the Pandava king touched his hand with his own hand, and all the others with Vasudeva at their head saluted him.

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau vṛddhāv abhivādya halāyudhaḥ yudhiṣṭhireṇa sahita upāviśad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Halayudha, the subduer of foes, paid homage to the elders Virata and Drupada, and then sat down together with Yudhishthira.

sanskrit: tatas teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu pārthiveṣu samantataḥ vāsudevam abhiprekṣya rauhiṇeyo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Then, when the kings had sat down on all sides, Rauhineya gazed upon Vasudeva and spoke:

sanskrit: bhavitāyaṃ mahāraudro dāruṇaḥ puruṣakṣayaḥ diṣṭam etad dhruvaṃ manye na śakyam ativartitum
english: "There will be a great and terrible slaughter of men—this I regard as fated and certain; it cannot be averted.

sanskrit: asmād yuddhāt samuttīrṇān api vaḥ sasuhṛjjanān arogān akṣatair dehaiḥ paśyeyam iti me matiḥ
english: My wish is that I might see you, along with your dear ones, emerge safe from this battle, healthy and with bodies unharmed.

sanskrit: sametaṃ pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ kālapakvam asaṃśayam vimardaḥ sumahān bhāvī māṃsaśoṇitakardamaḥ
english: The assembled royal Kshatriya clan is ripened by Time without doubt; a great crushing is coming, a mire of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: ukto mayā vāsudevaḥ punaḥ punar upahvare saṃbandhiṣu samāṃ vṛttiṃ vartasva madhusūdana
english: Again and again in private I urged Vasudeva: 'Madhusudana, maintain equal conduct toward your kinsmen on both sides.'

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā hi yathāsmākaṃ tathā duryodhano nṛpaḥ tasyāpi kriyatāṃ yuktyā saparyeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: "'The Pandavas are as much ours as is king Duryodhana; show him too the proper honor'—this I urged again and again.

sanskrit: tac ca me nākarod vākyaṃ tvadarthe madhusūdanaḥ niviṣṭaḥ sarvabhāvena dhanaṃjayam avekṣya ca
english: But Madhusudana did not heed that counsel of mine; he was wholly committed with all his being, with eyes fixed on Dhananjaya.

sanskrit: dhruvo jayaḥ pāṇḍavānām iti me niścitā matiḥ tathā hy abhiniveśo 'yaṃ vāsudevasya bhārata
english: Victory of the Pandavas is certain—this is my firm conviction; for such indeed is the absorption of Vasudeva, O Bharata.

sanskrit: na cāham utsahe kṛṣṇam ṛte lokam udīkṣitum tato 'ham anuvartāmi keśavasya cikīrṣitam
english: And I cannot bear to witness the world without Krishna; therefore I shall follow what Keshava intends to do.

sanskrit: ubhau śiṣyau hi me vīrau gadāyuddhaviśāradau tulyasneho 'smy ato bhīme tathā duryodhane nṛpe
english: For both are my heroic pupils, skilled in mace-fighting; my affection is equal for Bhima and for king Duryodhana.

sanskrit: tasmād yāsyāmi tīrthāni sarasvatyā niṣevitum na hi śakṣyāmi kauravyān naśyamānān upekṣitum
english: Therefore I shall go to visit the sacred fords along the Sarasvati; I cannot bear to stand by as the Kauravas perish."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur anujñātaś ca pāṇḍavaiḥ tīrthayātrāṃ yayau rāmo nivartya madhusūdanam
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed Rama, with the permission of the Pandavas, departed on his pilgrimage to the sacred fords, taking leave of Madhusudana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu bhīṣmakasya mahātmanaḥ hiraṇyalomno nṛpateḥ sākṣād indrasakhasya vai
english: Vaishampayana said: At that very time, the son of the great-souled Bhishmaka, king of the golden-fleeced, who was himself a friend of Indra—

sanskrit: āhṛtīnām adhipater bhojasyātiyaśasvinaḥ dākṣiṇātyapateḥ putro dikṣu rukmīti viśrutaḥ
english: the son of that lord of abundance, the exceedingly glorious Bhoja, lord of the southern regions—known in all directions as Rukmi—

sanskrit: yaḥ kiṃpuruṣasiṃhasya gandhamādanavāsinaḥ śiṣyaḥ kṛtsnaṃ dhanurvedaṃ catuṣpādam avāptavān
english: he who was the pupil of the lion among Kimpurushas who dwells on Gandhamadana, and had mastered the complete four-footed science of archery,

sanskrit: yo māhendraṃ dhanur lebhe tulyaṃ gāṇḍīvatejasā śārṅgeṇa ca mahābāhuḥ saṃmitaṃ divyam akṣayam
english: the mighty-armed one who obtained the bow Mahendra, equal in splendor to the Gandiva, and the divine inexhaustible Sharnga which is on a par with it—

sanskrit: trīṇy evaitāni divyāni dhanūṃṣi divicāriṇām vāruṇaṃ gāṇḍivaṃ tatra māhendraṃ vijayaṃ dhanuḥ
english: these three are the only divine bows that traverse the heavens: the Varuna bow called Gandiva, the Mahendra called Vijaya,

sanskrit: śārṅgaṃ tu vaiṣṇavaṃ prāhur divyaṃ tejomayaṃ dhanuḥ dhārayām āsa yat kṛṣṇaḥ parasenābhayāvaham
english: and Sharnga, they say, the Vaishnava bow, divine and made of pure radiance—which Krishna bore, striking terror into enemy armies.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaṃ pāvakāl lebhe khāṇḍave pākaśāsaniḥ drumād rukmī mahātejā vijayaṃ pratyapadyata
english: The son of Paka's slayer received the Gandiva from the fire in the Khandava forest; the greatly splendid Rukmi obtained Vijaya from a tree.

sanskrit: saṃchidya mauravān pāśān nihatya muram ojasā nirjitya narakaṃ bhaumam āhṛtya maṇikuṇḍale
english: Having severed the bonds of Mura, having slain Mura by force, having conquered Naraka the earth-born, and having recovered the jeweled earrings,

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśa strīsahasrāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca pratipede hṛṣīkeśaḥ śārṅgaṃ ca dhanur uttamam
english: Hrishikesha recovered sixteen thousand women and various jewels and the supreme bow Sharnga.

sanskrit: rukmī tu vijayaṃ labdhvā dhanur meghasamasvanam vibhīṣayann iva jagat pāṇḍavān abhyavartata
english: But Rukmi, having obtained the bow Vijaya whose sound was like a thundercloud, came to the Pandavas as though threatening the whole world.

sanskrit: nāmṛṣyata purā yo 'sau svabāhubaladarpitaḥ rukmiṇyā haraṇaṃ vīro vāsudevena dhīmatā
english: This hero, proud of the strength of his own arms, had in the past not forgiven the abduction of Rukmini by the wise Vasudeva.

sanskrit: kṛtvā pratijñāṃ nāhatvā nivartiṣyāmi keśavam tato 'nvadhāvad vārṣṇeyaṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam
english: Having made the vow "I shall not return without slaying Keshava," he then pursued the Vrishni hero, foremost among all weapon-bearers.

sanskrit: senayā caturaṅgiṇyā mahatyā dūrapātayā vicitrāyudhavarmiṇyā gaṅgayeva pravṛddhayā
english: With a great four-fold army, far-reaching, equipped with varied weapons and armor, swollen like the flooding Ganga,

sanskrit: sa samāsādya vārṣṇeyaṃ yogānām īśvaraṃ prabhum vyaṃsito vrīḍito rājann ājagāma sa kuṇḍinam
english: he encountered the Vrishni hero, lord and master of yogas, was utterly defeated and humiliated, O king, and returned to Kundina.

sanskrit: yatraiva kṛṣṇena raṇe nirjitaḥ paravīrahā tatra bhojakaṭaṃ nāma cakre nagaram uttamam
english: Right there where he had been defeated in battle by Krishna, the slayer of enemy heroes, he built a fine city named Bhojakata.

sanskrit: sainyena mahatā tena prabhūtagajavājinā puraṃ tad bhuvi vikhyātaṃ nāmnā bhojakaṭaṃ nṛpa
english: With that great army rich in elephants and horses, that city became renowned on earth by the name Bhojakata, O king.

sanskrit: sa bhojarājaḥ sainyena mahatā parivāritaḥ akṣauhiṇyā mahāvīryaḥ pāṇḍavān samupāgamat
english: That Bhoja king, of great valor, surrounded by a great army comprising a full akshauhini division, came to the Pandavas.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kavacī khaḍgī śarī dhanvī talī rathī dhvajenādityavarṇena praviveśa mahācamūm
english: Then, clad in armor, bearing sword and arrows and bow and palm-shield, riding his chariot, with a banner the color of the sun, he entered the great host.

sanskrit: viditaḥ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ vāsudevapriyepsayā yudhiṣṭhiras tu taṃ rājā pratyudgamyābhyapūjayat
english: Known to the Pandavas, and desiring to please Vasudeva, king Yudhishthira went out to meet him and honored him.

sanskrit: sa pūjitaḥ pāṇḍusutair yathānyāyaṃ susatkṛtaḥ pratipūjya ca tān sarvān viśrāntaḥ sahasainikaḥ uvāca madhye vīrāṇāṃ kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Duly honored and well-received by the sons of Pandu, he honored them all in return; then, rested, along with his soldiers, he spoke in the midst of the heroes to Dhananjaya, son of Kunti:

sanskrit: sahāyo 'smi sthito yuddhe yadi bhīto 'si pāṇḍava kariṣyāmi raṇe sāhyam asahyaṃ tava śatrubhiḥ
english: "I stand ready as your ally in battle. If you are afraid, O Pandava, I shall render you in combat an assistance that your enemies cannot withstand."

sanskrit: na hi me vikrame tulyaḥ pumān astīha kaś cana nihatya samare śatrūṃs tava dāsyāmi phalguna
english: "For there is no man in this world equal to me in valor; slaying your enemies in battle, I shall give them to you, O Phalguna."

sanskrit: ity ukto dharmarājasya keśavasya ca saṃnidhau śṛṇvatāṃ pārthivendrāṇām anyeṣāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: Addressed thus, in the presence of the king of dharma and Keshava, and with all the lords of the earth and everyone else listening,

sanskrit: vāsudevam abhiprekṣya dharmarājaṃ ca pāṇḍavam uvāca dhīmān kaunteyaḥ prahasya sakhipūrvakam
english: the wise son of Kunti glanced at Vasudeva and at the Pandava king of dharma, and spoke laughing in a tone of friendly warmth:

sanskrit: yudhyamānasya me vīra gandharvaiḥ sumahābalaiḥ sahāyo ghoṣayātrāyāṃ kas tadāsīt sakhā mama
english: "Hero, when I was fighting the exceedingly mighty Gandharvas during the cattle-raid expedition, who was my ally, who was my friend then?

sanskrit: tathā pratibhaye tasmin devadānavasaṃkule khāṇḍave yudhyamānasya kaḥ sahāyas tadābhavat
english: Likewise in that terrifying encounter in the Khandava forest, filled with gods and demons—who was my ally when I fought then?

sanskrit: nivātakavacair yuddhe kālakeyaiś ca dānavaiḥ tatra me yudhyamānasya kaḥ sahāyas tadābhavat
english: In battle against the Nivatakavachas and the Kalakeya demons—who was my ally when I fought there?

sanskrit: tathā virāṭanagare kurubhiḥ saha saṃgare yudhyato bahubhis tāta kaḥ sahāyo 'bhavan mama
english: Likewise in Virata's city, when I fought many Kurus in battle—who was my ally then, dear friend?

sanskrit: upajīvya raṇe rudraṃ śakraṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ yamam varuṇaṃ pāvakaṃ caiva kṛpaṃ droṇaṃ ca mādhavam
english: Taking shelter in battle upon Rudra, Shakra, Vaishravana, Yama, Varuna, Pavaka, Kripa, Drona, and Madhava—

sanskrit: dhārayan gāṇḍivaṃ divyaṃ dhanus tejomayaṃ dṛḍham akṣayyaśarasaṃyukto divyāstraparibṛṃhitaḥ
english: bearing the divine Gandiva bow, made of pure radiance and firm, furnished with inexhaustible arrows, and augmented by celestial weapons—

sanskrit: kauravāṇāṃ kule jātaḥ pāṇḍoḥ putro viśeṣataḥ droṇaṃ vyapadiśañ śiṣyo vāsudevasahāyavān
english: born in the lineage of the Kauravas, and above all as the son of Pandu, pointing to Drona as my teacher, I am the pupil who has Vasudeva as ally.

sanskrit: katham asmadvidho brūyād bhīto 'smīty ayaśaskaram vacanaṃ naraśārdūla vajrāyudham api svayam
english: How could one such as I speak the inglorious words 'I am afraid'—even were the thunderbolt-wielding Indra himself my enemy, O tiger among men?

sanskrit: nāsmi bhīto mahābāho sahāyārthaś ca nāsti me yathākāmaṃ yathāyogaṃ gaccha vānyatra tiṣṭha vā
english: I am not afraid, O mighty-armed one, nor do I have any need of an ally. Go wherever you wish, however you see fit, or remain elsewhere."

sanskrit: vinivartya tato rukmī senāṃ sāgarasaṃnibhām duryodhanam upāgacchat tathaiva bharatarṣabha
english: Then Rukmi turned back with his ocean-like army and went to Duryodhana in the same manner, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tathaiva cābhigamyainam uvāca sa narādhipaḥ pratyākhyātaś ca tenāpi sa tadā śūramāninā
english: And having approached him likewise, he said the same things to that king, and was equally rejected by him who thought himself a hero.

sanskrit: dvāv eva tu mahārāja tasmād yuddhād vyapeyatuḥ rauhiṇeyaś ca vārṣṇeyo rukmī ca vasudhādhipaḥ
english: Two thus withdrew from that war, O great king: Rauhineya the Vrishni hero, and Rukmi the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: gate rāme tīrthayātrāṃ bhīṣmakasya sute tathā upāviśan pāṇḍaveyā mantrāya punar eva hi
english: With Rama departed on his pilgrimage to sacred fords, and the son of Bhishmaka likewise withdrawn, the Pandavas sat down once again to take counsel.
